zebralogic.title: Assign fixed‑position attributes immediately
zebralogic.principle: If a clue directly states that a specific attribute value belongs to a particular house number, assign that value to that house right away, reducing the search space.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When parsing clues that contain explicit house numbers such as “in the first house”, “the second house”, “the fifth house”, etc.
zebralogic.example: Failing to assign “Arnold is in the fourth house” immediately, leaving unnecessary ambiguity.

zebralogic.title: Translate adjacency constraints into offset constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that X is directly left/right of Y, enforce that X and Y occupy adjacent houses with the specified direction. When a clue says X and Y are next to each other (adjacent without direction), enforce adjacency but allow either ordering.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions adjacency, either with a direction (left/right) or with phrasing like “next to each other”, “adjacent”, “side by side”.
zebralogic.example: Treating “X and Y are next to each other” as X directly left of Y, fixing the order incorrectly.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: A clue stating “N houses between X and Y” means there are exactly N houses separating X and Y, i.e., the absolute difference in positions is N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two items.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting “two houses between X and Y” as a distance of 2 instead of the correct distance of 3.

zebralogic.title: Bind equivalence clues to the same house
zebralogic.principle: If a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., “The milk drinker has a hamster”), treat them as belonging to the same house, linking the attributes together.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue directly connects two attribute values across categories.
zebralogic.example: Failing to bind “the painting hobby = the camping vacation”, causing them to be placed in different houses.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Clues that say X is somewhere left/right of Y impose only an ordering (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)), not adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses phrasing like “somewhere to the left of”, “somewhere to the right of”, without specifying adjacency.
zebralogic.example: Assuming “X is somewhere left of Y” means X is directly left of Y, which over‑constrains the puzzle.

zebralogic.title: Apply exclusion constraints
zebralogic.principle: When a clue forbids an attribute from a specific house (e.g., “Peter is not in the fifth house”), eliminate that possibility from the candidate set for that house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains negation or exclusion language.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring “The person who uses a Huawei P50 is not in the fifth house”, allowing Huawei P50 to be placed in house 5.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; after assigning a value, remove it from the possibilities for other houses.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same music genre to two different houses, violating the one‑per‑category rule.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: When outputting the final solution, write each attribute value exactly as it appears in the problem, preserving spelling and case.
zebralogic.example: Changing “hip hop” to “Hip Hop”, causing a mismatch with the reference answer.

zebralogic.title: Make forced assignments when only one candidate remains
zebralogic.principle: If after applying all constraints a house (or an attribute) has exactly one possible remaining value, assign it immediately.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After each round of constraint propagation.
zebralogic.example: Not assigning a child to a house when it is the only remaining option, leaving unnecessary ambiguity.

zebralogic.title: Validate final answer completeness and JSON structure
zebralogic.principle: Before submitting, ensure the JSON object is syntactically complete, contains all houses, and follows the required schema.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After constructing the final answer, before output.
zebralogic.example: Omitting the last house row, resulting in an incomplete JSON that fails verification.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats the number of houses mentioned as the positional offset rather than the count of houses separating the two items.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that ‘N houses between X and Y’ means |pos(X) − pos(Y)| = N + 1, not N.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats linked attributes as independent, missing the forced co‑location.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue equates two attribute values, record them as a single combined entity that must occupy the same house.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may place the same value in multiple houses when constraints are not fully propagated.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After each assignment, remove that value from the candidate lists of all other houses in the same category.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model normalises text automatically, changing capitalisation or spacing.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute strings exactly as they appear in the problem statement when producing the final grid.

zebralogic.description: Treating 'next to each other' as a directed adjacency (assuming a specific order)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model conflates the undirected phrase “next to each other” with a directed “directly left/right of”, imposing an unnecessary ordering constraint.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Interpret “X and Y are next to each other” as simply ‘adjacent’, allowing both possible left‑right orders and letting other clues resolve the direction.
